geometry_edits.rationale: Soften the base connector to let the ground edge read as a public threshold rather than a sealed plinth.
Reduce the width of the ground spine so the void can register as usable space.
Open the split further to create a clearer court-like opening.
Increase the void size so the building reads less like two colliding boxes and more like one organized mass with public relief.
Orient the perforation along the horizontal frontage to better acknowledge the access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Reduce the ground spine emphasis so the frontage can become a clearer public threshold rather than a heavy base seam.
Narrow the base connector to lighten the anchor and make room for a more legible carved public void.
Widen the separation enough for the split to read as a usable court-like opening rather than a collision gap.
Deepen the puncture so the void becomes more legible across views and better supports the public-space brief.
Align the perforation to reinforce a stronger horizontal public seam connected to the street edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact split block with a simple overall mass idea, so the dominant gesture is understandable in all views, but it remains too box-like and only weakly differentiated into a public ground condition. The blue access edge is not answered by a convincing entry seam, court, or undercut; the mass largely seals the frontage instead of making a neighborhood threshold. The central notch/void is shallow and reads more as a minor separation between two volumes than a usable public space. Sectionally, the object does not yet express a clear active base with calm upper hierarchy; the split-wing gesture is present but not developed into an inhabitable civic ground figure. Programmatically this is only partially compatible with neighborhood living: it has the compactness and modest height, but not the active edge/public void logic that the brief requires.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too tower-like and vertical for this compact neighborhood-living mass; risks reading as an office tower rather than an active ground-oriented building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing can create a strong dominant silhouette with clear sectional hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks a comparable carved court or atrium; the reference is much more explicitly void-driven.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved central void can organize the mass and give a legible public interior figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much flatter and more ground-responsive; candidate is over-compact and too sealed at the access edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low, clear street-facing base with a distinct public threshold supports neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate does not yet achieve that continuous sectional promenade or usable public void.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/ramp/terrace logic can bind a neighborhood-scale mass into one continuous spatial figure.

warnings: Reject as program-fit hard fail: the visible mass does not yet establish an active ground threshold or legible public void at the access edge.
The form is coherent, but the void is too small and semantically weak to satisfy neighborhood public-space expectations.
Avoid over-rewarding the split silhouette; it currently reads as two colliding boxes more than one continuous spatial rule.
